    },
    {
      "login": "maflcko",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "noted typos and grammatical errors in comments"
    },
    {
      "login": "l0rinc",

      "note": "Approach NACK over mixing consensus behavior changes with refactoring; raised performance concerns"
    },
    {
      "login": "darosior",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Concept ACK, but flagged dropped script execution caching in TestBlockValidity as a regression"
    },
    {
      "login": "svanstaa",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "ran reindex-chainstate benchmarks confirming no slowdown with par=1"
    },
    {
      "login": "Eunovo",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK and full ACK; suggested code and comment improvements"
    },
    {
      "login": "fanquake",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "r:3895419081",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "combining consensus-critical behavior change with structural refactoring increases the risk of subtle consensus bugs",
      "quote": "Approach NACK. The recent consensus bug in the BIP110 soft fork proposal in this exact area indicates we need to be extra careful, which isn't the case in this PR yet. I left a ton of suggestions as I",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "l0rinc maintained the Approach NACK arguing the PR should be split and opened alternative PR #34875",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2919590624",
        "c:4040558208",
        "c:4060763295",
        "c:4243866329",
        "c:4244738537"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4244508717",
      "status_by_quote": "The updated results don't change my review - my objections are about mixing a behavior change with a refactor in consensus-critical code, not performance."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:4054825361",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "potential single-threaded validation performance regression from using checkqueue with no worker threads",
      "quote": "what makes you say this doesn't introduce any regression? I've been trying to measure the -assumevalid=0 -par=1 case for almost a week now. master finished in 60 hours; this branch is still running...",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "benchmarks confirmed no performance regression",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4060763295",
        "c:4243866329"
      ],
      "other_replies": [
        "c:4105727071",
        "c:4189159560"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4191667067",
      "status_by_quote": "I managed to run -par=1 on a different server, it has very similar performance."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:4075771363",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "dropping script execution caching in TestBlockValidity introduces validation delays at block submission time",
      "quote": "Besides, i think this is a regression to remove script execution caching from TBV. This introduces additional delay at block submission time, doing work that was already performed at block template ge",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "fjahr restored script caching in TestBlockValidity",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4112120612"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:4112120612",
      "status_by_quote": "I have now re-introduced caching in the same commit and fixed the commit message accordingly."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2103422435",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "make CCheckQueueControl work with 0 worker threads and always use it to unify single-threaded and multithreaded script checking",
      "quote": "An alternative would be to make CCheckQueueControl work with 0 worker threads (maybe it already does?) and just always use it. That would completely unify the approach here.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "implemented by author after benchmarking confirmed no penalty",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:2989224515",
        "c:3831778712"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:3831778712",
      "status_by_quote": "Checkqueue can run without worker threads as well but I still expected that some changes would be needed. That doesn't seem to be the case, it seems to work well as is."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2103434017",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "populate pvChecks outside CheckInputScripts so CheckInputScripts can also call PrepareInputScriptChecks without duplicating checks",
      "quote": "did you consider the alternative approach of doing the pvChecks population not here (but in ConnectBlock() or a separate function), so that CheckInputScripts could also call PrepareInputScriptChecks and there would be no duplication of the coinbase check, cache check and TxData init?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author pushed updated version adopting the suggestion",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:2989224515",
        "rc:2157704941"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2157704941",
      "status_by_quote": "I have implemented this at the cost of duplicating the cache entry calculation."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2103526405",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "whether it is intended behavior that mining RPCs add entries to the script cache only in the -par=1 case",
      "quote": "I wonder if the current behavior is intended - it seems very strange to me that mining rpcs would add entries to the script cache, but only in the -par=1 case.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "theuni replied that it is very unlikely to be intended, and caching was later analyzed and restored",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4112120612"
      ],
      "other_replies": [
        "rc:2152860968",
        "rc:2152862922"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2152860968",
      "status_by_quote": "I think it's very unlikely that that behavior is intended :)"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:3593597789",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "eliminate the separate single-threaded path and create a checkqueue without workers",
      "quote": "Looking at this patch, I am asking myself why we're keeping the single threaded / no checkqueue case in the first place. This seems to introduce a vector of jobs for both cases now, so maybe we could just create a queue without any workers?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author implemented checkqueue without worker threads",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:3831778712"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:3831778712",
      "status_by_quote": "Checkqueue can run without worker threads as well but I still expected that some changes would be needed. That doesn't seem to be the case, it seems to work well as is."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2889037362",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "encapsulate cache access methods inside ValidationCache rather than extracting a local helper",
      "quote": "I could get behind properly encapsulating the cache and exposing only the contains/insert methods",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added methods to ValidationCache in a separate commit",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2919604231"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2919604231",
      "status_by_quote": "I agree that it is nicer to this in ValidationCache, I have taken these changes as a separate commit"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2889644265",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "return the cache key instead of a boolean to avoid recomputing the cache entry hash",
      "quote": "It returns a bool, which forces us to recompute the cache key. What if we adjust it to return the cache key instead",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author changed the function to return the hash",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2919600058",
        "rc:2919600869"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2919600058",
      "status_by_quote": "I have changed this function to return the hash so we don't have to recalculate it."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:4191667067",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "add upfront test coverage demonstrating thread-mode behavior before refactoring",
      "quote": "Missing upfront test coverage to demonstrate no behavior change - see my alternative which adds thread-mode tests first before any refactoring, so regressions are caught immediately.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author noted that existing functional and fuzz tests already cover -par=1 and declined to duplicate tests",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4243866329"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4243866329",
      "status_by_quote": "The functional tests already have -par=1 coverage and the fuzz test also use 0 worker threads in deterministic mode so I think this doesn't make a huge difference"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4070363347",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "document the trade-off that script cache entries are missed if a block fails validation",
      "quote": "Some txs that should be cached here will be missed if the block fails for any reason... I wonder if we should document the trade-off here.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author agreed to document this on the next retouch",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4072436193"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4072436193",
      "status_by_quote": "Thanks, I will tackle this when I have to retouch."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:2895813848",

      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",

    {
      "id": "c:6209971440",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "",

      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Added review suggestions and questions raised across the discussion under the current rules, and recorded fanquake's Concept ACK. darosior's regression concern was fixed and l0rinc's benchmark objection accepted, while l0rinc's Approach NACK regarding separating behavioral changes from refactoring remains contested.",
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "reviewer",
      "what": "further review after fanquake cc'd marcofleon and Eunovo approved",
      "id": "c:6210073640"
    },

      "on": "author",
      "what": "document script caching trade-off when retouching",
      "id": "rc:4072436193"
    }
  ]
}

claims.text: combining consensus-critical behavior change with structural refactoring increases the risk of subtle consensus bugs
claims.quote: Approach NACK. The recent consensus bug in the BIP110 soft fork proposal in this exact area indicates we need to be extra careful, which isn't the case in this PR yet. I left a ton of suggestions as I
claims.status_note: l0rinc maintained the Approach NACK arguing the PR should be split and opened alternative PR #34875
claims.status_by_quote: The updated results don't change my review - my objections are about mixing a behavior change with a refactor in consensus-critical code, not performance.

claims.text: potential single-threaded validation performance regression from using checkqueue with no worker threads
claims.quote: what makes you say this doesn't introduce any regression? I've been trying to measure the -assumevalid=0 -par=1 case for almost a week now. master finished in 60 hours; this branch is still running...
claims.status_by_quote: I managed to run -par=1 on a different server, it has very similar performance.

claims.text: dropping script execution caching in TestBlockValidity introduces validation delays at block submission time
claims.quote: Besides, i think this is a regression to remove script execution caching from TBV. This introduces additional delay at block submission time, doing work that was already performed at block template ge
claims.status_note: fjahr restored script caching in TestBlockValidity
claims.status_by_quote: I have now re-introduced caching in the same commit and fixed the commit message accordingly.

claims.text: make CCheckQueueControl work with 0 worker threads and always use it to unify single-threaded and multithreaded script checking
claims.quote: An alternative would be to make CCheckQueueControl work with 0 worker threads (maybe it already does?) and just always use it. That would completely unify the approach here.
claims.status_note: implemented by author after benchmarking confirmed no penalty
claims.status_by_quote: Checkqueue can run without worker threads as well but I still expected that some changes would be needed. That doesn't seem to be the case, it seems to work well as is.

claims.text: populate pvChecks outside CheckInputScripts so CheckInputScripts can also call PrepareInputScriptChecks without duplicating checks
claims.quote: did you consider the alternative approach of doing the pvChecks population not here (but in ConnectBlock() or a separate function), so that CheckInputScripts could also call PrepareInputScriptChecks and there would be no duplication of the coinbase check, cache check and TxData init?
claims.status_note: author pushed updated version adopting the suggestion
claims.status_by_quote: I have implemented this at the cost of duplicating the cache entry calculation.

claims.text: whether it is intended behavior that mining RPCs add entries to the script cache only in the -par=1 case
claims.quote: I wonder if the current behavior is intended - it seems very strange to me that mining rpcs would add entries to the script cache, but only in the -par=1 case.
claims.status_note: theuni replied that it is very unlikely to be intended, and caching was later analyzed and restored
claims.status_by_quote: I think it's very unlikely that that behavior is intended :)

claims.text: eliminate the separate single-threaded path and create a checkqueue without workers
claims.quote: Looking at this patch, I am asking myself why we're keeping the single threaded / no checkqueue case in the first place. This seems to introduce a vector of jobs for both cases now, so maybe we could just create a queue without any workers?
claims.status_note: author implemented checkqueue without worker threads
claims.status_by_quote: Checkqueue can run without worker threads as well but I still expected that some changes would be needed. That doesn't seem to be the case, it seems to work well as is.

claims.text: encapsulate cache access methods inside ValidationCache rather than extracting a local helper
claims.quote: I could get behind properly encapsulating the cache and exposing only the contains/insert methods
claims.status_note: author added methods to ValidationCache in a separate commit
claims.status_by_quote: I agree that it is nicer to this in ValidationCache, I have taken these changes as a separate commit

claims.text: return the cache key instead of a boolean to avoid recomputing the cache entry hash
claims.quote: It returns a bool, which forces us to recompute the cache key. What if we adjust it to return the cache key instead
claims.status_note: author changed the function to return the hash
claims.status_by_quote: I have changed this function to return the hash so we don't have to recalculate it.

claims.text: add upfront test coverage demonstrating thread-mode behavior before refactoring
claims.quote: Missing upfront test coverage to demonstrate no behavior change - see my alternative which adds thread-mode tests first before any refactoring, so regressions are caught immediately.
claims.status_note: author noted that existing functional and fuzz tests already cover -par=1 and declined to duplicate tests
claims.status_by_quote: The functional tests already have -par=1 coverage and the fuzz test also use 0 worker threads in deterministic mode so I think this doesn't make a huge difference

claims.text: document the trade-off that script cache entries are missed if a block fails validation
claims.quote: Some txs that should be cached here will be missed if the block fails for any reason... I wonder if we should document the trade-off here.
claims.status_note: author deferred addressing the documentation trade-off until next touch

claims.text: why the code was extracted into a separate function
claims.quote: Why is this made a separate function?
claims.status_note: author explained it improves readability and makes behavior changes easier to review
claims.status_by_quote: I just found it nicer in terms of documentation and readability to extract this into a function. It isn't strictly necessary but it should make the actual behavior change easier to review IMO.

support.reason: This seems like a nice cleanup, will look at it in detail later.
The changes simplify the flow for script verification in ConnectBlock, and they have a nice side effect of simplifying txvalidationcache_tests.cpp.
